items.text: There is no single correct exam for every applicant.
Check each program's current policy directly before committing months of prep to either exam.
Once the program requirement question is settled, or if a program genuinely accepts both, this is the honest fit test that most comparison articles skip in favour of generic advice.
Text Completion and Sentence Equivalence questions are essentially vocabulary-in-context tests, and that skill is coachable but slow to build if it is not already there.
GRE Quant stays closer to a solid school-level foundation and gives you more time per question relative to GMAT's tighter, adaptive pacing.

blocks.heading: What Counts As a Competitive Score

items.text: Score targets get repeated online without context constantly.

A combined Verbal + Quant score of roughly 320+ is generally seen as competitive for well-ranked engineering and computer science MS programs, with Quant carrying more weight for technical fields and a more balanced score mattering more for programs with a research or writing component.

Programs that accept GRE for MBA admissions typically look for a percentile-equivalent score comparable to their published average GMAT range, so check the school's GRE conversion guidance directly rather than assuming a fixed number applies everywhere.

blocks.heading: Four Questions Before You Commit Prep Months

items.text: The four questions narrows it down to what genuinely applies to your specific applications and timeline.
Before anything else, check the actual admissions page of every program on your shortlist for whether they require, prefer, or simply accept each exam.
Once the requirement question is settled, or if both exams are genuinely accepted, run one honest test: take a free official practice section of each.

blocks.heading: Mistakes to Avoid When Making This Decision

items.text: Acceptance of GRE for MBA admissions has expanded to the majority of business schools worldwide.
Some MS programs, particularly in the US, have dropped GRE requirements entirely, while others still require it strictly by department even within the same university.

A slightly easier prep experience is a weak trade if it produces a score the admissions committee weighs less confidently, especially at programs like ISB where GMAT submissions still dominate admitted batches.

blocks.heading: GRE Vs GMAT At a Glance
rows: Built primarily for
Graduate school admissions across MS, PhD, and a fast-growing share of MBA programs.
Business school admissions: MBA, Master's in Finance, Master's in Management, and other management degrees.
Sections
Analytical Writing, two Verbal Reasoning sections, two Quantitative Reasoning sections.
Verbal Reasoning, Quantitative Reasoning, Data Insights (GMAT Focus Edition, no essay).
Total duration
About 1 hour 58 minutes.
About 2 hours 15 minutes.
Adaptivity
Section-adaptive: your score on the first Verbal or Quant section decides the difficulty of the second one in that measure.
Question-adaptive within each section: difficulty shifts after almost every question based on your answers.
Score range
260-340 total (Verbal and Quant each 130-170), Analytical Writing scored separately 0-6.
205-805 total, each of the three sections scored 60-90 on the same scale.
Score validity
Reportable for 5 years from the test date.
Reportable for 5 years from the test date.

blocks.heading: Programs Actually Require Which Exam
rows: MS/MEng in engineering, computer science, data science (US, Canada, Europe)
GRE is the default and, in most cases, the only accepted exam.
PhD programs (any field, most countries)
GRE, where a score is required at all; many PhD programs have dropped standardized testing entirely, so check the specific department.
Top global MBA programs outside India (M7, most T20 US and European schools)
Both accepted and scored on equal footing in the vast majority of programs; GMAT is still the more common submission among applicants, not a hard requirement.
ISB (Indian School of Business)
GRE is accepted, but the large majority of admitted applicants still submit GMAT scores, so GMAT remains the safer default here.
IIM flagship two-year MBA (PGP) for domestic candidates
Neither GRE nor GMAT is used. Admission runs through CAT (or XAT for XLRI), a completely separate exam track.
IIM one-year and executive MBA programs
Both GRE and GMAT are accepted, alongside CAT/XAT scores for some batches.
